definition: mean number of letters per word
rationale: LLMs prefer longer words (e.g. 'utilize' instead of 'use').

definition: share of words with 8 or more letters
rationale: Same 'fancier vocabulary' tendency, less affected by a few very long words.
Vocabulary richness: AI text tends to repeat the same words more.

definition: share of words that are NLTK English stopwords
rationale: Function-word usage is a classic authorship signal that is hard to fake.

definition: mean number of tokens per sentence (sent_tokenize)
rationale: LLM sentences cluster around a comfortable medium length.

definition: standard deviation of tokens per sentence
rationale: Humans mix very short and very long sentences; AI is more uniform.
AI polishing adds clauses and lists, so more commas.
Overall punctuation density differs between human and machine text.

definition: 1 if the text contains '!', else 0 (as in LAB6)
rationale: Exclamations are a human, emotional trait that AI editing removes.
Questions to the reader are typical of conversational human text.

definition: 1 if the text contains an em or en dash, else 0
rationale: Em dashes are a well-known LLM habit.
Original layout (lists, headings) is often merged into prose by AI editing.
Dates, figures and references are dropped or rounded during rewriting.

definition: words starting with a capital letter / words
rationale: Proper nouns and names reflect factual, human-sourced text.
Personal voice is a human trait that AI rewriting tends to neutralise.
Polishing expands contractions; humanisers may add them back.

definition: words from our AI_WORDS list per 100 words
rationale: Words like 'additionally', 'crucial', 'ensure' are over-used by LLMs.
